MUQATIL:75:8-18/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:8-18/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:8-18/r4.claim: On that day a person is told what they sent ahead for the afterlife and what good or evil they left after death for others to follow.

FARRA:v3p210/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p210/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p210/r7.claim: What a person sent ahead is prior work; what was left behind includes a practice others continue, whose reward or sin remains undiminished.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p333#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p333#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p333#4/r1.claim: Qatada says the person is shown what acts of obedience he sent ahead and what obligations to God he left behind.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334/r1.claim: Ibn Masud interprets what a person left behind as a good or evil practice that people continued after him.

NAHHAS:v5p81/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p81/r4.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p81/r4.claim: Qatada says a person is told what obedience he sent ahead and which obligations he left; Ibn ʿAbbās says it includes all good and evil.

SULAMI:v2p361#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p361#2/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p361#2/r1.claim: Five afflictions in sin are worse than the sin: abandonment by God, loss of the saints' qualities, closed mercy and opened punishment, being seen while disobeying, and standing before God with one's ugly deeds exposed.

THALABI:v10p85/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p85/r1.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p85/r1.claim: A report through Atiyya from Ibn Abbas says what was sent ahead means sins, while what was left behind means acts of obedience.

THALABI:v10p85/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p85/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p85/r2.claim: Mujahid says the person is informed of the first and last deed performed.

THALABI:v10p85/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p85/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p85/r3.claim: Qatada says it is the obedience sent ahead and God's due postponed and neglected.

THALABI:v10p85/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p85/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p85/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the deeds sent ahead may be good or bad, while what is left behind includes obedience a person failed to perform.

THALABI:v10p85/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p85/r5.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p85/r5.claim: Ata interprets what is sent ahead and left behind as deeds from the beginning and end of life.

THALABI:v10p85/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p85/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v10p85/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says it means the wealth spent for oneself and the wealth left to heirs.

THALABI:v10p85/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p85/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p85/r7.claim: The discussion is linked to the verse saying each soul will know what it sent forward and left behind.

THALABI:v10p85/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p85/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد بن أبي بكر
THALABI:v10p85/r8.claim: Abu Said lists five harms of sin worse than the sin: divine abandonment, loss of the saints' qualities, closed mercy and opened punishment, God's witnessing the sin, and public reckoning of one's offenses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r15.claim: A person is told about good and evil deeds performed before death that become known after death.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r16.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r16.claim: The person is told of sins committed earlier and obedience left for later.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r17.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r17.claim: It may mean the person's first and last deeds.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r18.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r18.claim: It may mean earlier evil and later good.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r19.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r19.claim: It may mean obligatory duties performed and duties omitted.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r20.claim: It may mean what a person did for this world and what he deferred for the afterlife.

QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r2.claim: On that day a person is informed of deeds sent ahead or left behind, including sins God recorded even if the person forgot them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r1.claim: What a person sent ahead is any deed done in life; what was left behind is a good or bad practice followed after death.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r2.claim: What was sent ahead is what a person did for himself, while what was left behind is what he left to heirs.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد وعطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r3.claim: They apply both terms to a person's lifetime: deeds from the early part of life and deeds from its later part.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r4.claim: What was sent ahead is obedience performed; what was left behind is a duty to God neglected or not performed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r5.claim: What was sent ahead is good or evil performed, and what was left behind is obedience not performed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p491#2/r6.claim: He links this wording to the statement that each soul will know what it sent ahead and left behind.

JISHUMI:v10p7180/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r11.claim: Nabaʾ means a report of great significance.

JISHUMI:v10p7180/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r12.claim: Taqdīm means placing something before another, the opposite of delay; precedence can be temporal, spatial, or by rank.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r10.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r10.claim: Qatada reads the clauses as obedience to God and neglect of a due owed to God, respectively.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r11.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r11.claim: Mujahid interprets the clauses as a person’s first and last deeds.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r12.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r12.claim: Ata says it means deeds in the first and last parts of a person’s life.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r13.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r13.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says it is wealth spent for oneself versus wealth left to heirs.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r8.claim: They say a person is told what good and bad he did before death and what good or bad precedent continued afterward.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r9.claim: Atiyya reports Ibn Abbas’s alternative: ‘sent ahead’ means disobedience and ‘left behind’ means obedience.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r7.claim: A person is told of deeds done and left undone, wealth given away or left as an inheritance, good and evil acts, and good or bad practices continued by others; Mujahid says it means one's first and last deeds.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r2.claim: بما قدم وأخر comprehensively includes every deed, which the person finds fully recorded.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud interpret it as deeds done in life and a continuing practice left behind.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses it as sins committed earlier and acts of obedience deferred.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says it means wealth spent for oneself and wealth left to heirs.

TABRISI:75:12-14/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:75:12-14/r5.claim: People are told about their earliest and latest deeds.

TABRISI:75:12-14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:12-14/r6.claim: Other views include deeds begun in life and continued after death, sins committed and duties neglected, what a person did and left, or wealth sent ahead to oneself and wealth left to heirs.

TABRISI:75:12-14/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r7.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:75:12-14/r7.claim: The report can mean duties a person performed for God and duties delayed and wasted.

TABRISI:75:12-14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TABRISI:75:12-14/r8.claim: Another view distinguishes property given for oneself from property left to one's heirs.

TABRISI:75:12-14/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:12-14/r9.claim: A nabaʾ is consequential information; the term fits because only deeds that deserve requital count here, not acts as inconsequential as if they never existed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r1.claim: A person is told what they did before death and what they set in motion for others to do after death.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r2.claim: The person is informed of their first and last deeds.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r3.claim: The person is informed of evil deeds done early and good deeds postponed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r4.claim: The person is informed of the obligatory deeds performed and those left undone.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r5.claim: Another, unattributed interpretation contrasts past disobedience with delayed obedience.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#3/r6.claim: The person is informed of what they spent and what they left to heirs.

RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r1.claim: One interpretation is what a person sent ahead in deeds he performed and what he left behind in deeds he did not perform.

RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r2.claim: Mujāhid interprets the phrase as the beginning and end of a person's deeds.

RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r3.claim: The most apparent time for this disclosure is the Resurrection during presentation, reckoning, and weighing of deeds, though it may also occur at death when a person's destination is shown.

RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r4.claim: Another interpretation contrasts wealth given away with wealth left as inheritance.

RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#3/r5.claim: A third interpretation is good or evil deeds and a good or bad practice that continued after the person.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r10.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r10.claim: Al-Qushayri says the disclosure occurs at the Resurrection when deeds are weighed, though it could occur at death.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r11.claim: Qurtubi prefers disclosure at the weighing of deeds, citing reports that good works continue to accrue after death.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r12.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra lists knowledge taught, a good child, a copied Quran, a mosque, a travelers’ shelter, a water channel, and charity as benefits that continue after death.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r5.claim: The human is told what good or evil he advanced and what good or evil practice he left to continue after him.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r6.claim: Mujahid and al-Nakha‘i say the person is told of his first and last deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas, shared by Qatada, says he advanced disobedience and delayed obedience.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the first as money spent for oneself and the later as what one leaves to heirs.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r9.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says it means duties performed and duties left for later.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r1.claim: The wording “after his death while in his grave” shows that the full disclosure is not at death but at the weighing in the afterlife, although he may receive good news in the grave.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r2.claim: The later burdens others bear include the burdens of those misled without knowledge, supporting disclosure after deeds are weighed.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:75:7-13/r3.claim: A report in Sahih says whoever starts a good practice receives its reward and the reward of later practitioners, while whoever starts an evil practice bears its sin and theirs.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#4/r1.claim: The person will be told about the deeds he performed and what he left undone.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r1.claim: Zayd b. Aslam says what one sent ahead from wealth benefits oneself, while what one leaves behind goes to the heir.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r2.speaker: النخعي ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r2.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi and Mujahid interpret what was sent ahead and left behind as a person’s first and last deeds.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r3.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the pair as obligatory duties performed and duties neglected.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p347/r4.claim: The wording should be taken generally, encompassing all acts mentioned by exegetes and others they did not mention.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p277/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p277/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p277/r5.claim: Each person is informed of every deed, old or recent and small or great, as another verse says all deeds will be present.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p246/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p246/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p246/r1.claim: The passive yunnabbaʾ foregrounds disclosure of hidden deeds rather than who discloses them and emphasizes that the task is easy for God.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p246/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p246/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p246/r2.claim: What a person sent ahead and left behind can mean all early and late deeds, preferring law over desire, unfinished acts cut short by death, or deeds personally done versus beneficial or harmful practices others continue; Ibn Abbas holds the last interpretation, followed by al-Ghazali.

BURSEVI:v10p191/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191/r1.claim: The one who informs at the reckoning may be God, an angel acting by His command, or the record of deeds as it is unfolded.

BURSEVI:v10p191/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191/r2.claim: “What he sent ahead” can mean any good or evil deed he performed; “what he left behind” can mean good or evil he failed to do, or deeds whose effects continued after him.

BURSEVI:v10p191/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191/r3.claim: Other interpretations take the paired terms as good and evil deeds later acted upon by others, wealth given in charity versus wealth left by inheritance, endowment, or bequest, or the first and last deeds.

BURSEVI:v10p191/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191/r4.speaker: عبد الله الأنصاري
BURSEVI:v10p191/r4.claim: Abdullah al-Ansari urges repentance before death and sending wealth ahead as charity, since retaining it brings regret.

BURSEVI:v10p191/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191/r5.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p191/r5.claim: The Prophet says every person will meet the Lord without interpreter or veil, see only their own deeds on either side and Hell ahead, and should ward off the Fire even with half a date.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r1.claim: Most interpreters say a person is told what they did and left undone, whether good or bad; another view contrasts deeds done with good or evil practices set in motion and followed later.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r2.claim: Ibn Masud explains what is advanced and delayed as one's deeds and one's precedent, good or bad, that others continue after.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reads it as wealth spent for oneself in life versus wealth left to heirs, increased, endowed, or bequeathed.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد والنخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r4.claim: Mujahid and al-Nakhaʿi explain the two terms as the first and last of a person's deeds.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person advanced sins and delayed obedience; Qatada and Ikrima transmit a similar interpretation, which fits a wicked person.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#3/r6.claim: This sentence is separate from the preceding clause because each stands independently, and from the next clause to expose the severity or the person's bad state.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r5.claim: The person is told what he is and what his good or evil consists in; his deeds and true condition are disclosed.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r6.claim: “What he sent ahead and left behind” can mean earlier and later deeds, or all good and bad acts sent ahead for the afterlife or left undone; all are accounted for.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r5.claim: The announcement that a person will be told his deeds is an explanatory resumption prompted by the final return, or an inclusive substitute for it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r6.claim: Although everyone is informed of deeds, ‘the human’ here means the disbeliever addressed by the context; similar wording in different Qur'anic settings need not have one referent.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r7.claim: Being informed of what one did is a metonym for receiving its recompense: the deed is identified, exposing and rebuking its doer.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p347/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p347/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p347/r1.claim: What a person brought forward means what he did; what he left behind includes duties or prohibitions left unfulfilled, as in the Prophet's supplication for forgiveness.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p347/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p347/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p347/r2.claim: The passage advances from the report of deeds to the disbeliever's awareness of them through bodily testimony and the opened record of actions.

TABATABAI:75:11-15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r6.claim: What a person did earlier and later in life, or before death and through a good or bad practice continued afterward, is disclosed and recompensed.

TABATABAI:75:11-15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r7.claim: Reported alternatives include deeds done versus good or bad deeds left undone; early sins versus later obedience; obedience followed by neglect of God's due; or wealth spent on oneself versus left to heirs. The author finds these remote.

ASAD-NOTES:75:11#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:11#n4/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:75:11#n4/r1.claim: The phrase means all the good and bad deeds one performed or omitted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.claim: Verses 7-15 answer demands to hasten Judgment: when upheaval arrives no one can flee except to God, and each must answer for every deed despite attempts to conceal it.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r2.claim: Although people may offer excuses to escape punishment, each person will in truth testify against himself and cannot conceal the truth.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r2.claim: The deeds reported as sent ahead and left behind are disbelief and turning away on one side, and delayed faith and prayer on the other.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r4.claim: The surah repeatedly pairs opposites or corresponding matters: Resurrection with the reproachful soul, sun with moon, deeds advanced with delayed, inward self-knowledge with outward excuses, and immediate life with afterlife.

STUDYQURAN:75:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:13/r1.claim: Verse 13 echoes 82:5; what people sent ahead may mean all their deeds or only good deeds that testify for them and earn reward.

STUDYQURAN:75:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:13/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:13/r2.claim: What a person leaves behind may mean good deeds not done in life or good deeds that continue to bear fruit.

STUDYQURAN:75:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:13/r3.speaker: a famous ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:75:13/r3.claim: A person who establishes a good practice receives its own reward and an equal reward for later followers; one who establishes an evil practice bears its burden and theirs.
